flashcards.front_prompt: Who is Neem Baba and how does he interact with Amber in Chapter 7?
flashcards.back_answer: Neem Baba is a personified, talking neem tree in Amber's courtyard. When Amber rests under his shade after school, he greets her warmly and shares his ancient origins, historical spread across India, and self-sacrificing medicinal benefits. Memory Trigger: 🌳 An ancient neem tree smiling at a schoolgirl.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Personification creates an affectionate dialogue that instills environmental respect in students.

flashcards.front_prompt: Why is the Neem tree traditionally celebrated as a 'Village Pharmacy'?
flashcards.back_answer: Because every part of the neem tree provides zero-cost natural health remedies: 1) Leaves treat skin diseases and purify air. 2) Twigs (datun) maintain dental hygiene. 3) Bark cures fever. 4) Seed oil heals wounds and acts as an eco-friendly organic pesticide for farm crops.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Neem provides comprehensive, sustainable healthcare remedies for rural and urban households.

flashcards.front_prompt: What is the meaning, phonetic guide, and contextual usage of 'Purifies'?
flashcards.back_answer: Definition: Cleanses, filters, or frees from harmful pollutants and impurities. Phonetic: /ˈpjʊə.rɪ.faɪz/. Textual Sentence: 'The neem tree purifies the air around our homes.' Original Usage: 'Boiling water purifies it by killing harmful bacteria.' Synonyms: Cleanses, sanitizes, filters, decontaminates. Antonyms: Pollutes, contaminates, taints.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Purifies means removing contaminants to restore health and cleanliness.

flashcards.front_prompt: Explain Compound Words (Closed, Open, Hyphenated) with examples from Chapter 7.
flashcards.back_answer: Rule: Compound words are formed by joining two or more base words. 1) Closed Compounds (written as one word): courtyard, doorstep. 2) Open Compounds (written with a space): neem tree, rice flour. 3) Hyphenated Compounds (joined by a hyphen): cost-effective, eco-friendly.
flashcards.key_takeaway: Compound words unite individual terms to create distinct new meanings.
